headline: P0054 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share runs well above peers at every complexity level, including patients with 0-1 chronic conditions
rationale: P0054 billed 99215 on 16.3% of 355 claims. Given this panel's patient complexity, about 4.2% would be expected, and the risk-adjusted score is 4.16. The higher share is not explained by a sicker panel. Most visits (232 of 355) are for patients with 0-2 chronic conditions, and the provider's 99215 share is above the all-provider share in every stratum. For patients with 0 conditions it is 8.6% vs 2.1%, and for 1 condition 11.2% vs 3.4%, roughly 3-4x peers. In the 4-condition stratum the gap is small (18.2% vs 13.9%). The sampled low-complexity 99215s are mostly for single routine problems: low back pain alone (C0023884), abdominal pain (C0023893), UTI (C0023958), and stable single conditions such as hyperlipidemia (C0023651, C0023704, C0023769). The same patient was billed 99215 for COPD twice (C0023676, C0023971). Patient P0054-N0034 was billed 99215 for back pain (C0023884) and 99213 for a rash two days later (C0023775). The sampled 99215s on 4+ condition patients (e.g., C0023740, C0023749) look plausible. Overall this pattern is consistent with upcoding concentrated in lower-complexity visits, not with a high-acuity panel. The claim lists are samples, and no clinical documentation, time records or MDM notes are included, so level of service cannot be confirmed.
next_steps: Request medical records (MDM documentation and total time) for the sampled 99215s on 0-1 condition patients, starting with C0023884, C0023893, C0023958, C0023651 and C0023676/C0023971.
Check whether the documentation supports high-complexity MDM or 40+ minutes of total time under the 2021+ E/M guidelines.
Pull the full set of 99215 claims on low-complexity patients, not just the sample, to measure how widespread the pattern is.
Review the 99214-heavy mix (220 of 355 claims) for the same issue, since 99214 is the dominant code and the screen measured only 99215.
Compare against payer audit history, and check for templated or cloned notes and for modifier-25 or same-day procedure stacking.
